summary: Verified 6.6, NOT on par: the sensitivity blocker kemdo-C2-B1 is confirmed. The base splash face is a fully band-wrapped oval with no eave, slit or eyes (mummy read), and the Highrim splash head is a blank white egg. Both cards ship in the shop, loading and collection screens. The splash-finish major is confirmed, with one correction: the figure fills about 60-78% of the frame height, not a third. It reads small by area and composition, and it is posterized and lit differently from the plate. All four minors were reproduced or kept. Re-run now: the crown gate passes 3/3 (R3 13.9 cm, top 2.117) and the robe spring chains are present. The gameplay model is close to par; the score is held down by the cards. Hoods are rounded, and I found no other sensitivity problem, horror read or pointed hood. The lens-under-bar leftover is not_measured rather than still_open. Frame timing was not measured.

findings.title: Base and Highrim splash faces read as a wrapped mummy and a blank egg
findings.what: Base splash.png: inside the rounded hood the face is a pale oval of horizontal wrap bands, with no brow eave, no ink slit and no eyes; it reads as a mummy at card and full size. kemdo_highrim_splash.png: head tipped to the sky, a featureless white oval. Long Evening splash, the portraits (portrait.png shows the eye slit with living eyes) and the icon are fine.
findings.evidence: Viewed art/out/fighters/kemdo/splash.png and kemdo_highrim_splash.png at 1600x900 plus _harness/_shots/closing_kemdo_c2b_splash_head_x4.png and closing_kemdo_c2b_hr_head_x4.png; files last changed in 8b93ac403 (Nov 3). Splashes ship: src/ui/screens/shop.tsx:206 (Portrait kind=splash), plus loading and collection screens.
findings.gauge: A LoL splash makes a covered face read as a living person: eyes and brow lit as the focal point.
findings.fix: Re-pose base and Highrim splash heads (pitch <= 10 deg up, 3/4 to camera) so the sandstone eave and warm eye slit show, add the portrait camera's warm under-eave bounce, add a splash head-crop QA (eye-slit contrast) and re-render those two cards.
findings.verifierNote: Could not refute. The blank-wrapped face is unambiguous at 1:1, and the standing rule (owner_rulings.md:6 faces read alive; ruling 2 'reads blank ... at portrait size') covers it. Shipped asset, so blocker stands. Hood itself is rounded, not pointed.

findings.title: Splash cards are posterized 3D cut-outs with flat light that does not match the plate
findings.what: All three splashes paste a posterized, stair-stepped 3D render onto a painted plate; figure and plate do not share light or brushwork, and the base card lacks the brief's lens-into-the-sun hero beat. Correction: the figure is not 'a third of the frame height' - by eye in the 1600x900 files the body spans about y 290-880 (base, ~65%), 270-810 (Highrim, ~60%), 110-810 (Long Evening, ~78%); it is narrow (~15-20% of width) and pushed to the right third, so it reads small by area, not by height.
findings.evidence: art/out/fighters/kemdo/splash.png, kemdo_highrim_splash.png, kemdo_long_evening_splash.png viewed at full size; stair-step edges in _harness/_shots/closing_kemdo_c2b_splash_head_x4.png and closing_kemdo_c2b_hr_head_x4.png.
findings.gauge: A LoL splash is one painted image: the champion dominates the frame and shares light, rim and brushwork with the backdrop.
findings.fix: Render the subject at full resolution without posterize, key it from the plate's sun with a warm rim, run one paint pass over plate and figure together, widen the figure's share of frame area (closer camera, dynamic diagonal pose); base pose per brief.
findings.verifierNote: Core claim (cut-out, posterized, light mismatch) reproduced; the 'one third of frame height' figure is wrong (60-78% by height), so the fix's 60-75% height target is already met - the problem is area, composition and finish. Severity stays major.

findings.gauge: LoL recall loops keep props clear of the face.
findings.fix: Rotate the glaive ~20 deg outward and move the lens ~12 cm forward in the recall bake; add recall to the zero-penetration gate.
